description.narrative: At the project level, IFCs financial support to the BPC 2025-2029 modernization plan will directly improve the performance of its distribution assets. Notably, the construction of the Pangbang Station will address the reliability of power in the Pangbang area for its 5,292 customers, who remain vulnerable to frequent power interruptions due to long-distance low voltage distribution lines passing through dense forests and adverse weather conditions. Furthermore, the establishment of the four regional DCCs (integrated into the central DCC) can enhance the reliability of power supply through integrating Advance Distribution Management System, which enables online monitoring of distribution activities across the key nodes in distribution system, with better detection and restoring capabilities for system faults. At the market level, IFC's investment will provide BPC with the necessary fundings to meet with the growing domestic electricity demand and to integrate the planned 1.9 GW of new generation capacity scheduled for commissioning between 2025 and 2029.

IFC is considering providing a local currency-linked senior loan facility of up to US$20 million, supported by local currency hedging from the International Development Association (IDA) Private Sector Window (PSW) Local Currency Facility (LCF), to Bhutan Power Corporation Limited (BPC or the Borrower) to fund part of its capital expenditure program over the next few years, particularly for two sub-components: (i) the construction of Panbang Gas Insulated Substation (GIS) and (ii) the upgradation of 4 regional Distribution Control Centers (DCC) and connection to Central DCC in Thimphu (each sub-component, individually Sub-project and collectively as the Project).
